name: Loop condition written against username.length() counts as 'multiple indices' even if the increment is missing/wrong vs only guaranteed-terminating loops count
side_a: Do not deduct when the loop header tests an index variable against `username.length()` (e.g. `while (i < username.length())` or `while (i <= username.length())`), even if some branch forgets to advance `i` so the loop could spin forever — the header itself shows the code is indexing over multiple positions of username, which satisfies 'in the context of a loop that considers multiple parts or indices'.
side_b: Deduct whenever termination is not actually guaranteed — a branch that leaves `i` unchanged makes the loop no better than `while (true)` with no reliable exit, so 'no other conditions stop the loop appropriately' applies.

name: Out-of-bounds indexing / non-compiling body ignored vs loop must be legal and in-bounds
side_a: Do not deduct for index-arithmetic or compile errors inside the loop — `username.charAt(i + 1)` with `i <= username.length()` (guaranteed StringIndexOutOfBounds), iterating a String with an enhanced for, or calling a nonexistent method — the credit is for structuring the traversal as a loop over characters of username, not for its correctness.
side_b: Deduct when the loop cannot actually run over username's parts because it indexes past the end or uses constructs that do not compile, so no multiple indices are really examined.

name: Hyphen located through genuine String API calls vs. String treated as a char array / non-existent String methods
side_a: If the response reaches the hyphen through real String API calls on the instance variable — e.g. username.charAt(i) compared to '-' with username.length() bounding the scan — award B2 (no_deduct), even if the loop bounds or index arithmetic are buggy (off-by-one, infinite loop, i+1 out of range); those errors are judged under B3/B4.
side_b: If the response never makes a valid String method call to find the hyphen — iterating the String as if it were an array/collection (for (char c : username)) and/or invoking a method that does not exist on String (username.delete(...)) — deduct B2: no String method has been called correctly to identify the hyphen's location.

name: Char-by-char accumulation that selects the right characters vs. lookahead (`charAt(i+1)`) offsets that drop a letter or keep the hyphen
side_a: No_deduct when the character-by-character build appends exactly the non-hyphen characters of the username in order — the test and the index advance line up so that the hyphen (and only the hyphen) is skipped and every letter is appended exactly once.
side_b: Deduct when the response tests a lookahead character (`username.charAt(i + 1) == '-'`) but then skips/advances on the *current* index, so the accumulated result drops the letter immediately before the hyphen, re-appends or retains the hyphen itself, or never advances at all. This is an algorithmic defect in which pieces of the string are combined, not an excused method-call or compile slip.

name: Misusing a String method's arguments/name vs. treating String as an iterable/mutable container
side_a: No_deduct when the response uses real String behavior (immutable, indexed access or substring) and merely garbles a call's name or arguments while the intended construction of the returned string is clear.
side_b: Deduct when the response builds the answer by treating `username` as an array/collection or mutable object — e.g. enhanced-for iteration over a String or calling a mutator on it — so there is no valid String-based construction of the shortened name to credit.
